editorial: Killers of the Flower Moon, a period crime thriller, turns an oil rush into a living nightmare, the sort of terror that grinds behind the surface of progress. The film arches over 1920s Oklahoma with a quiet, relentless dread that mimics the slow burn of a conspiratorial storm. With Joaquin Phoenix carrying every scene with almost no dialogue, his silence becomes a vicious heartbeat. Only the pacing feels a little slack, turning a few crucial moments into slow singlets amid the otherwise taut rhythm. Ideal for viewers drawn to historical dramas that expose systemic injustice.
targetAudience: Ideal for viewers drawn to historical dramas that expose systemic injustice.
